messages:
sophie-support: Hey team, customer REPORT-4832 (apac fintech) sees p95/p99 token generation latency spike starting ~2026-03-16T03:00Z. They say requests go from ~80ms to 1.2s and sometimes 2.5s. No errors, just slow. x-rw-trace-id they attached: trace-0a1b2c3d. Can someone eyeball routing?

kai-eng: thanks, Sophie. I pulled their sample request: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-RW-Trace: trace-0a1b2c3d" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" --data '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}'

kai-eng: On our edge logs the request hits ap-southeast-2 edge (~03:00Z) then we see a hop to an intermediate egress IP that belongs to our eu-west aggregator for a few seconds, then to us-west, then back to a local inference pool. That explains multi-region RTT.

trace-bot: trace-0a1b2c3d: 
  hops: [ap-se-edge -> 52.64.11.8 (AS12345, apac provider) -> 3.122.45.19 (AS54321, eu transit) -> 18.205.77.33 (AS67890, us-east) -> 10.10.20.5 (redwood-private)]

allan-sre: that path is odd. We should not be going via eu transit for APAC->US backhaul. Maria, any recent BGP or peering changes?

maria-netops: I rolled a peering policy tweak to prefer a new partner (AS54321) for redundancy earlier that morning. Looks like the community tag we set accidentally had higher local-pref for APAC prefixes than intended — so APAC edge is preferring the eu transit for some customer prefixes.

kai-eng: can you paste the exact community we set? maybe we flipped the sign.

maria-netops: config snippet: 
```
route-map REDUNDANCY permit 10
 set community 54321:100 additive
 set local-preference 200
```
We intended that for only a small subset but the match clause was too broad. So APAC->EU path became preferred for many prefixes.

sophie-support: oh. That would explain spikes — extra ~120-200ms per extra hop plus variability. Customer wants a root-cause and a mitigation now.

allan-sre: mitigation options: 1) revert the route-map globally (fast, broad) 2) tighten match to exact customer prefixes (safer) 3) add short-term policy on ap-se edges to prefer direct backbone (surgically). I'm leaning to (3) for lowest blast radius. Any objections?

akash-obs: I can push a change to ap-southeast-2 edge only to set local-pref 300 for our internal backbone prefixes within 5 minutes and monitor. I'll also add a temporary alert for p95 > 300ms for that customer.

maria-netops: I'll prepare the rollback for the earlier change and schedule an after-action. Also opening a ticket with the transit provider — AS54321 — to flag unexpected propagation.

kai-eng: action items: Akash pushes edge pref change (ETA 5m), Maria reverts broad route-map (ETA 20m), Allan to watch p95/p99 and confirm reduction, Sophie to update customer with mitigation + ETA.

sophie-support: sending quick note now: "We observed an unexpected routing propagation that caused some APAC requests to transit through EU/US and back, increasing latency. We're applying an edge-level routing preference now and will confirm when p95 improves; estimated <30m. Will follow up with RCA." :thumbsup:

trace-bot: new alert: p95 for REPORT-4832 in ap-southeast-2 spiked to 1.9s at 03:07Z, then dropped to 120ms at 03:12Z after policy change.

allan-sre: confirmed. Looks good. Maria please capture the exact AS path before/after and timeframe for RCA. Also include traceroute samples from the customer's IP if they can provide them.

maria-netops: captured AS paths and timestamps, will post in incident tracker INC-2026-013 and link back. Will include BGP dump and config diff.

sophie-support: customer updated and very happy with the quick mitigation. Closing escalation unless we find further anomalies. Thanks all.

akash-obs: saving trace artifacts: s3://observability/traces/REPORT-4832/trace-0a1b2c3d.log

kai-eng: follow-up: add unit test to route-map deploy pipeline to prevent broad matches from going out without approval.

sophie-support: noted. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
